## Summary
`complete_window` silently drops the caller's payload when a head already exists and `replace_existing` was not requested. Replaying your own completion and losing the window to another MCP client returned **identical** responses, so a client that ran a model and produced real output had no way to know it was dropped.

Adds an optional `skipped_reason` to the response. Purely additive — no change to `window_created`, `head_superseded`, or the data model, and **no per-client canvas fork**: the chain stays keyed on `(watcher_id, granularity, window_start)`.

skipped_reason?: 'replayed_own_completion' | 'completed_by_other_client' | 'already_completed'

`events.client_id` is FK'd to `oauth_clients`, so `complete-window.ts:452-457` nulls any unregistered id: **PAT and device callers store NULL**, and a manual-open window may carry no run id. So in many real calls neither side has an identity.

Both hit on 2026-07-30 while shipping #2370. `pi-review` is a REQUIRED check, so
a broken reviewer blocks merge outright.

## Codex quota

`make review` (default `REVIEWER_CLI=auto` → codex outside a codex harness) died
with `ERROR: You've hit your usage limit … try again at Aug 5th, 2026`. The gate
**fails closed on purpose** and will not silently fall back to another reviewer.

Switch explicitly: `REVIEWER_CLI=claude CLAUDE_REVIEW_MODEL=fable make review`.
`review_validate_claude_model` accepts only `fable`, `opus`, or `claude-opus-*`
(`scripts/lib/review-reviewer.sh`) — matching [[feedback_use_fable_for_review]].

**Still exhausted on 2026-07-31** (same Aug 5 reset), hit again on lobu #2387.
`make review-fix` dies the same way and takes the *same* env override —
`REVIEWER_CLI=claude CLAUDE_REVIEW_MODEL=fable make review-fix`. Its failure is
quiet: it prints `(no summary emitted)` and `Error 1`, which reads like "nothing
to fix" rather than "the reviewer never ran". Always check the HEAD of its output
for the quota line before believing a clean fixer pass —
[[project_review_harness_codex_single_point]].

## The claude reviewer's $schema rejection

```
Error: --json-schema is not a valid JSON Schema: no schema with key or ref
"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"
```

`scripts/review.sh` passes `prompts/review-output-schema.json` verbatim via
`--json-schema`, and the Claude CLI's validator does not resolve that meta-schema
ref. Nothing to do with the diff under review.

Workaround — **working tree only, never commit it** (it belongs in its own PR,
not whatever branch you're shipping):

```bash
cp prompts/review-output-schema.json /tmp/review-schema.bak
python3 -c "import json;p='prompts/review-output-schema.json';d=json.load(open(p));d.pop('\$schema',None);json.dump(d,open(p,'w'),indent=2)"
REVIEWER_CLI=claude CLAUDE_REVIEW_MODEL=fable make review
cp /tmp/review-schema.bak prompts/review-output-schema.json   # restore IMMEDIATELY
```

Dropping `$schema` removes only the meta-schema declaration; the constraint body
is unchanged, so the verdict is still schema-validated. Verify with `git status`
after restoring — a stray edit here would land in the next commit.

## Re-running review is sometimes mandatory, not a loop

`make review` posts `pi-review` against a specific SHA. If anything moves the
head — including the Codesmith bot pushing to your open PR branch — the new head
has no status and the PR sits `BLOCKED` with nothing explaining why. review.sh
detects this and refuses rather than attaching a verdict to a stale commit. That
re-run is not the find-fix loop [[feedback_review_is_last_gate_not_the_loop]]
warns about.

Two Lobu PRs can pin the same Owletto squash commit, so they share one Owletto PR — #2508 and #2511 did exactly that. The gate located *the* proof with `comments.find(c => c.body.startsWith(PROOF_MARKER))` and rewrote it in place via `upsertComment(..., PROOF_MARKER, ...)`, which matches on the same prefix. Whichever PR ran the gate last took the other's comment.

The marker is not an identity. The proof payload already carries `lobu_repo` and `lobu_pr`; this keys selection and the write on that instead.

Two failures this removes, both silent:

name: project_ui_review_proof_keyed_by_lobu_pr
description: "The ui-review gate used to find its proof comment by marker prefix, so two Lobu PRs pinning the same Owletto SHA silently stole each other's proof and reset each other's approval — fixed and MERGED as #2520 (53fbd02ae) on 2026-08-05"

Shipped 2026-08-05 as PR #2520, squash `53fbd02ae`. Closes the last unowned item
from the 14:45 pi session (`019fd262-d829-7617-b4c4-654e5ae74020`).

## The defect

`scripts/ui-review.ts` located the proof with
`comments.find(c => c.body.startsWith(PROOF_MARKER))` and rewrote it through
`upsertComment(..., PROOF_MARKER, ...)`, which matches the same prefix. Several
Lobu PRs can pin one Owletto squash commit and therefore share one Owletto PR —
#2508 and #2511 actually did. Whichever ran the gate last took the other's
comment. Two silent failures followed:

- The victim's gate reported `UI proof missing; rerun make ui-review with
  ARTIFACT=...` for a proof that existed and had been approved.
- The PATCH bumped `updated_at`, and `findApproval` only accepts comments newer
  than that — so an already-granted `/ui-approve` stopped counting.

## The fix

The marker is not an identity; the encoded payload already carries `lobu_repo`
and `lobu_pr`. `findProofComment(comments, lobuRepo, lobuPr)` in
`scripts/lib/ui-review-proof.ts` selects on those, and `upsertComment` now
delegates to `writeComment(repo, issue, existing, body)` so the proof path
updates the comment it selected by owner rather than by prefix.

**No "fail loudly on rebind" guard was added**, though the original proposal
asked for one. Once the key is right, overwriting another PR's proof is
unreachable — a runtime check would be dead code and score as slop. An
end-to-end test holds the property instead.

Verdict: bug_free 90, simplicity 92, slop 0, 0 blockers (claude/fable).

## Still open by design

`/ui-approve <owletto_sha>` is keyed by the Owletto SHA alone, so one admin
approval satisfies every Lobu PR pinning that SHA whose proof predates it. The
approved UI is byte-identical, so this is defensible — but it is a separate
decision from proof ownership and was deliberately left alone.

[[reference_check_drift_is_gated_by_ui_approve]],
[[reference_ui_review_screenshot_capture_recipe]]

description: "Live feed rows can carry keys their connector's feeds_schema never declared (Slack mints per-DM keys like slack:D0BEQTB3WFN), so counting declared feeds_schema keys under-counts real feeds — the unrealized gap left in PR #2516's event-trigger guard"

Verified against prod 2026-08-05 while reviewing #2516.

`connector_definitions.feeds_schema` is **not** the closed set of a connector's
feeds. Slack mints per-DM feed keys at runtime:

```
connector_key  feed_key
slack          slack:D0BEQTB3WFN
```

So any logic that counts `jsonb_object_keys(feeds_schema)` to decide "does this
connector have feeds" under-counts. #2516's `countDeclaredFeeds` does exactly
that, in the guard that rejects an event trigger on a connector with zero
declared events and zero declared feeds.

**Currently harmless, and that is the trap.** Every connector key whose
definition rows all declare zero `behavior_events` and an empty `feeds_schema`
— `apple.computer_use`, `os.shell`, `telegram`, plus archived `discord`,
`test.echo`, `webhook` — has **0** live feeds today. `chrome`, the connector the
reviewer named as the worry, declares 3 feeds and has 4 live ones, so the guard
never reaches it. The day one of the barren connectors gets a dynamic feed, the
guard blocks a legitimate `feed.auto_paused` trigger with "cannot drive an event
trigger".

Per [[feedback_row_counts_cannot_retire_a_code_risk]], the zero count does not
retire the defect — it only says it has not fired yet. Recorded on the PR as a
comment before merge (`9224fce77`).

## Query trap

`connector_definitions` has **multiple rows per key** (active + archived, several
versions — `x` appears 4×, `linkedin` 3×). Joining
`connector_definitions.key = connections.connector_key` matches the wrong
definition and manufactures false positives; my first pass "found" 29 orphaned
feeds that way. Aggregate per key first
(`GROUP BY key HAVING bool_and(...)`) before concluding anything.

Related: [[reference_connector_actions_live_in_the_db]],
[[reference_bundled_connector_action_count_matrix]]
